question: Which statement best describes Call hooks at the top level?
options: React remembers Hook values by the order of Hook calls. If that order changes, a value can attach to the wrong Hook. Numbered coat-check tickets are a useful analogy: each number must keep its place. Hook order is like numbered slots: React expects the same slot to hold the same state on every render.
Call each Hook near the start of a component, before early returns. This keeps the call order the same on every render. Think of filling numbered drawers in the same order each time.
Do not call Hooks inside an `if`, loop, or nested function. Those paths may run a different number of times. It is like moving items between numbered drawers and confusing the labels.
Call Hooks inside function components or custom Hooks, not regular helper functions. React needs to know which component owns the Hook. It is like using a key only with the lock it belongs to.
explanation: Call each Hook near the start of a component, before early returns. This keeps the call order the same on every render. Think of filling numbered drawers in the same order each time.
